_note: Every tunable number in the game. If a number appears in a .js file, it belongs here instead. Changing anything under 'climate', 'player.speed', or any site x/z means re-running the balance check.

world._scaleNote: One number for the size of the whole world. 1 is the nominal canyon: 600 m from end to end, 250 m across. Everything measured in metres multiplies by this at load. Deliberately NOT scaled: how fast you walk, how close you must stand to survey something, and anything vertical — you are the same size whatever the world does.
world._sunNote: sunElevationDeg drives three things at once and they must not drift apart: where the DirectionalLight sits, where the sun is drawn in the sky, and how far the west wall throws its shadow across the floor. The shadow a wall casts is height/tan(elevation) measured from its CREST, and the west crest now stands at x=230 — west.toe plus west.run — so the shaded stripe is roughly (230 - 78/tan(elev)) back to the floor's western edge. At 22 degrees that is about a quarter of the floor, which is where it was before the crevice was reshaped. Lower this and the stripe widens until shade stops meaning anything; raise it and it narrows to nothing. If you change west.height or west.toe, re-run npm run balance and check the shaded percentage rather than guessing.

palette._note: Ground colour, baked into the terrain mesh once at load. Costs nothing at runtime — change these freely. Each triple is r,g,b in 0..1. 'ash' is the flat ground, 'rock' is what steep slopes show, 'broadWarm' drifts the tone slowly across the map so large areas are not one flat colour.

canyon._note: The crevice: a split in the rock, not a bowl. TWO LAYERS, and the split between them is the whole design. The OUTER wall (west.toe / east.toe and the run, height and talus beside them) is the thing that keeps you in, and its toe line is a STRAIGHT LINE IN X that no other number here is allowed to move. The BUTTRESS in front of it carries every irregular thing — the pinching and opening, the notches, the wandering axis, the choke at the south end — and it is capped in height, so riding it up gets you a ledge and never a way out. WHY IT IS BUILT THIS WAY, because it is not obvious and it was measured: a wall line that moves in x as you walk along z is a diagonal ramp, and the square-root face does NOT stop it. Stand still on the wall while the wall slides sideways under you and the grade you feel is the wall's own grade times how fast the line moves. At about 0.03 metres of sideways drift per metre of length — far less than any interesting shape needs — that is a walkable 0.2, and a flood fill walked straight out of an earlier version of this crevice on exactly that route, gaining eight metres over a hundred metres of length without ever climbing anything. Pinning the containment toe and putting all the shape in a capped buttress in front of it is what buys the irregularity back.
canyon._widthNote: width is the NOMINAL floor width and is only used for reporting; the real floor edge at any z is west.toe minus the west buttress's thickness there, and likewise east. The buttress thickness is what widthVary swings, on a 3-octave field so the crevice pinches and opens on several scales at once instead of breathing like a sine wave. widthShare on each wall decides how much of that swing that side takes, so the two sides never move together. GAIN, and this catches everyone: the world's value-noise fbm does not swing plus or minus one — in practice it reaches about plus or minus 0.28 for three octaves. The gain brings each field up to full range so that the clamp in terrain.js is a real bound and widthVary/crestVary mean what they say. Raise a gain and the field spends longer pinned at its clamp, which flattens the extremes into plateaus.
canyon._notchNote: Side channels: places where the buttress is simply missing, so the floor runs back to the foot of the main cliff and dead-ends against it. Placed by one octave of noise read at a different LEVEL on each wall, so the two sides never notch at the same z and there is no list of features for heightAt to loop over. halfWidth is in noise units and sets how much length each notch spans; depth is the fraction of the buttress it removes. The main wall behind is untouched — that is what makes a notch a dead end rather than a door.
canyon._chokeNote: The south end closes by narrowing: the buttresses swell over the last stretch until the floor between them is only `leave` metres wide on each side. The north end does not — it is closed by collapse (see northEnd). Same result, different cause. start must stay north of anything placed at high z or a site ends up inside a buttress; spawn sits at z=240.
canyon._westNote: The west wall (+x) is the one that matters: the sun sits at +x, so this is the wall that throws the shaded stripe back across the floor, and the stripe at its foot is the last survivable ground on the map. It gets the dramatic profile — a short apron, a tall face whose gradient stays above the climb limit all the way to the crest, and a tall buttress in front of it. toe is where the containment face begins and is the one number in this block that must not be made to depend on z.
canyon._eastNote: The east wall (-x) is a talus slope: a long, walkable scree rising about fifteen metres, and only then the cliff. It is lower, it is set further back, and its crest line rides a different combination of the noise fields so the two walls do not rise and fall together. Walking up the scree is meant to be worth doing and is not a way out — the face above it still starts with a square root. Its buttress is deliberately LOW: keep it under talusHeight*height, about fifteen metres, so that standing on top of it never starts you higher up the main face than the scree would have.
canyon._endNote: The two ends do not match. North is the collapse — a rough, heaped face with boulders piled on it (see rockfall). South is the smooth narrowing the choke above has already begun. roughness is the lumpiness of the face; 0 is smooth. Both toe lines are straight in z for the same reason the wall toes are straight in x.
canyon._floorNote: The floor is broken but walkable. crossFall tips it across its width and the direction reverses along the length. The channel is a shallow braid of two threads wandering down the crevice on the slow field. The relief is then terraced into benchSteps low benches — the harder beds the water left standing — with benchEdge as the fraction of a step the riser occupies: 1 is the untouched ramp, smaller is a sharper bench, and below about 0.5 the risers stop being walkable. All of these are vertical or dimensionless and are NOT touched by world.scale, the same rule floorRelief already followed.

rockfall._note: The collapse that closes the NORTH end only — the south end chokes out instead, so there is nothing fallen there. These are the existing rough rocks at boulder scale, piled on the end slope so the block reads as fallen rock rather than as a hillside. They are decoration: the terrain underneath is what actually stops you, because nothing in this game has collision.

canyon._screeNote: Fallen material at the foot of the walls, in props.js. Each piece finds the foot of whichever wall stands at its z, measures how steep the rock above it is, and is kept with probability min(1, grade*steepBias)^steepPower — so the debris explains the cliff it came from: heavy under the west face, almost nothing under the east scree, which is not steep enough to shed anything. count is how many are CONSIDERED; roughly half of them survive that test and become meshes, and each one is a draw call, so raising it costs frame time. reach is how far out from the foot they spread.

sky._note: The sky gradient, baked into the sky shader at load. Triples are r,g,b in 0..1. 'haze' should stay close to render.fogColour — that match is what makes the ground fade into the sky instead of ending at a visible line. 'dither' hides banding in the gradient on 8-bit screens; set it to 0 to switch that off.
sky._note_glare: glareDepthTest: true means terrain hides the sun's glare, which is what you want in a canyon. Set false for the old open-plain behaviour where the glare always showed.

climate._note: The whole clock. dawn0 is where the dawn line starts in metres; dawnVelocity is metres per second. lethal is the temperature that kills a site. A site at x becomes lost at (x + (lethal + 12) / k - dawn0) / dawnVelocity seconds.
climate._graceNote: THE GRACE PERIOD. Mission time (S.t) does not advance until the clock starts, and until it does the dawn line does not move, no ground heats and nothing can be lost — every function in climate.js is a pure function of t and is simply handed a t that is not going anywhere. The world is not frozen, only the clock: grass, wind, gait, dust and the soundfield all ride S.animT, which runs from the first frame. backstopSeconds is the safety net for a player who never trips the story trigger; set it to 0 to remove the net entirely, in which case the clock only ever starts from the story. See src/game/clock.js.
climate._shadeNote: Shade is survival. Ground the west wall hides from the sun heats at (1 - shadeRelief) of the open rate, so it stays under the lethal line far longer — that shaded stripe is the only ground worth standing on once the dawn line has gone past. samples/stepMetres are the ray march toward the sun: samples*stepMetres must reach past the far wall or distant shadow is missed. softnessMetres is how many metres of penumbra the shadow edge gets instead of a hard line.

player._climbNote: maxClimbGrade is the steepest ground the suit will take, as a rise over run: 0.8 is about 39 degrees. The canyon walls are far steeper than this, which is what keeps you in the canyon — there is no invisible wall anywhere in this game.

hands._note: The first-person arms. rest* is arms down (barely out of frame); raise* is the scanner held up while surveying. Angles are radians: bigger shoulder swings the whole arm forward, bigger elbow folds the forearm up. leftBias and leftRaiseShare keep the two arms from being mirror images, which is what made them look wrong.

gait._note: The elbow base bend of 0.30 rad is load-bearing. A straight arm reads as a robot. gait.test.js asserts it never goes below this.

colour._note: Blade colour. 'tint' is the per-blade base (multiplied by a random 0.72-1.22 so no two blades match); 'root' is what the bottom of each blade is multiplied by, which is what gives the band depth instead of reading as flat green paper. 'rootHeight' is how far up the blade the root colour has faded out (0..1).

striders._note: The migration crosses the plateau beyond the north rim, not the canyon floor. herdZ/zStart/zRange are out past the end of the canyon; the animals are fifteen metres tall, so from the floor you see them over the rim before you hear where they are.

ashwaiters._note: Currently a damage radius, not a creature. Known issue 2 in HANDOFF.

sites._note: The six findings. Prose for each lives in story.json under the same id. duration is seconds of holding still to complete the survey.

camps._note: Only camp five is here. The Meridian moved across the planet for forty years, so camps one to four are somewhere else on this world and exist only in the record; their findings are recovered from the relay archive at the shelter — see shelter.archive. grantsSurvey is the one that matters: the camp carrying Vantaa's final entry is where the six findings are handed over, and reading it is what puts them on the manifest and starts the clock. Before it there is no manifest and nothing is expiring. Exactly one camp should carry this flag, and it must be one the player can actually reach.

graves._note: Only the deaths from the years they had stopped moving are buried here: raman (24), ruiz (31), vantaa (41). Okonkwo (9) and Demir (17) died while the survey was still travelling and are buried somewhere the player will never go. Their records still exist in story.json — that is where the answer key comes from — but their plates are not in this world, so nothing here states the year they died. g4 MOVED from x=-62 to x=-100 in the earned-manifest pass: at -62 it sat 6 m from the shortest walkable line between spawn and camp five, well inside its own 16 m read radius, so the player read it by walking past rather than by choosing to look. At -100 the walk passes 44 m away — 28 m clear of the radius — while the cairn stays in unobstructed line of sight from 71% of that walk. Seeing a marker and deciding to go to it is the whole point of an unmarked grave; being handed it is not.

shelter._note: The sixth camp. Only appears on the compass after camp five is read, and then only as '?'.
shelter._archiveNote: The relay terminal held everything the survey ever filed, because Lindqvist ran the relay. Each pair is [finding, which camp's record describes it] — the gift text is that camp's own line from story.json, so nothing new is written. Camp five carries the final entry and nothing else; loading four findings onto that beat would bury it.

chart._note: The chart is drawn as ink, not as filled squares: contour lines and hachures (the short downhill strokes ruled across a slope) carry the elevation, and everything unwalked is left blank. 'wobble' numbers are how unsteady the hand is, in pixels — 0 everywhere gives a clean drafted chart, higher gives a rougher field sketch. Nothing here is random: the same chart always draws the same way, so the PNG you export is the chart you were looking at.

palette._note: Ink on ground. Swap 'ground' for a pale paper tone and the ink colours for dark ones if you ever want it to read as paper rather than as a field display.

compass._note_labels: labelGapPx: minimum pixels between two compass labels. When sites cluster on one bearing, the nearer one keeps its text and the others show only an arrow.

deduction._note: The Meridian worksheet. minPerCommit is how many fates must be entered before the record will accept them — the point of it being more than one is that a player cannot test a single guess at a time and walk the answer out of the game. Three is the Obra Dinn number.
deduction._openingNote: openingGrave is the marker you land beside. Reading it fills that one row of the worksheet and leaves the other five empty. Nothing says anything about it — one filled row against five blank ones is the whole of the communication. Set it to null and the game starts with an empty sheet instead.
deduction._datesNote: datesFromRecord is the switch for the two crew whose graves are not in this world. Okonkwo (year 9) and Demir (year 17) died while the survey was still travelling, and NOTHING readable in this crevice states either year — the only place those dates appear is on their plates, which are elsewhere. So the worksheet cannot currently be completed for them, and it should not offer dates the player has no evidence for. Put the grave record ids here (e.g. ["g1","g2"]) ONLY once a log the player can actually reach states those years; the dates then become selectable when the shelter is read. Empty is the honest state until then.

textures._note: Every texture is drawn in code at load — there are no image files. Sizes are pixels per side: a 512 map costs about 1.4 MB on the graphics card, a 256 map about 350 KB. If the game runs slowly it halves all of these automatically (render.downgrade.textureScale) and redraws them. Setting 'enabled' false turns every generated map off and falls back to plain colours.

audio._note: Everything you hear is made from filtered noise at run time — there are no sound files. Gains are 0..1 and they add up, so raising several at once is how you get distortion. The wind is meant to sit under everything and only be noticed when it stops. Mute is V.

smoothing._note: Seconds for a level to travel most of the way to its target. Small is twitchy, large is syrupy. 'null' is deliberately quicker than the rest — the silence should arrive faster than it leaves.

wind._note: The floor. 'gain' is the level on flat, cool ground; elevation and heat add to it. Gusts are two slow sines beating against each other so the bed never loops audibly.

herd._note: Low-passed noise, panned by the same bearing the soundfield strip draws. 'curve' above 1 keeps it felt rather than heard until you are close: at half range it is a quarter as loud. Range itself comes from striders.audibleRange.

foot._note: One burst per footfall, fired off the gait phase so it lands with the foot rather than on a timer. 1.3g is in these numbers: low filter, slow decay, weight. 'phaseOffset' slides the hit earlier or later in the stride.

null._note: The ashwaiter silence. At full null everything is multiplied by zero — actual silence, not a quiet mix. 'curve' above 1 makes the drop bite earlier as you approach the den.

timing._note: fleetTransmissionDelayMs is measured from the moment the briefing's naming beat closes and the player steps outside — WALL clock, not mission time, so it fires whether or not the survey has been handed over yet. At 120000 (two minutes) it lands at about the point a player who walked straight to camp five is reading Vantaa's last entry, which may or may not be where it belongs. It is a placeholder block (story.fleetTransmission) and this is the one number that decides when it arrives.

render._lightNote: One warm key (the fixed low sun) and two cool fills. Keeping the key warm and the fills cool is what gives the ground shape; making them the same colour flattens it.

downgrade._note: Keep this path working. Target is 60fps on integrated graphics.

mobile._note: What a phone starts at, applied immediately instead of waiting to measure a stutter the player has already seen. These are RENDER-ONLY reductions: the world is still generated in full, so a phone and a desktop see the same rocks in the same places — only fewer of them are drawn. Set 'force' to true or false to override the automatic detection while testing on a desktop.

stick._note: The left thumb stick. radius is how far from where you first touched counts as full deflection; sprintAt is the fraction of that travel where walking becomes sprinting, because there is no shift key on a phone. deadZone stops a resting thumb from drifting.

props._note: Water and frost surfaces. water.depth is how far the surface sits above the LOWEST ground inside its radius — raise it and the pool spreads and deepens, lower it and it shrinks to nothing. frost.lift is how far the sheet floats above the ground it lies on.

_note_buildStamp: Shown small under the manifest. Bump this on every push — if the game on screen shows an older stamp than the newest push, the browser is serving a cached copy.
